RAJYA  SABHA
————
List of Questions for ORAL ANSWERS
to be asked at a sitting of the Rajya Sabha to be held on
Thursday, the August 3, 2006/Sravana 12, 1928 (Saka)
————
(Ministries :  Prime Minister;  Atomic Energy;  Coal;  Communications and
Information Technology;  External Affairs;  Housing and Urban Poverty
Alleviation;  Information and Broadcasting;  Overseas Indian Affairs;
Panchayati Raj;   Parliamentary Affairs;   Personnel, Public
Grievances and Pensions;  Planning;  Shipping, Road
Transport and Highways;  Space;  Statistics and
Programme  Implementation;   Urban
Development; Youth Affairs and Sports)
Total number of questions —20
Halting of nuclear tests
†*161. SHRIMATI MAYA SINGH:
Will the PRIME MINISTER be pleased to
state:
(a) whether differences between India
and USA regarding halting of nuclear tests
have been resolved;
(b) if so, the details thereof; and
(c) if not, the present status thereof?
Revival proposal of HDPEL
*162. SHRI TAPAN KUMAR SEN:
SHRI CHITTABRATA
MAJUMDAR:
Will the Minister of SHIPPING, ROAD
TRANSPORT AND HIGHWAYS be
pleased to state:
(a) the details of the revival proposal of
Hooghly Dock and Port Engineering Ltd.
(HDPEL);
(b) whether the same has been approved
by Board for Reconstruction of Public
Sector Enterprises (BRPSE);
(c) if not, the reasons therefor; and
(d) the action plan for improving the
order book position and cash flow
situation?
DDA land for schools and hospitals
†*163. SHRI PYARELAL
KHANDELWAL:
SHRI KALRAJ MISHRA:
Will the Minister of URBAN
DEVELOPMENT be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that DDA has
decided to sell plots for schools and
hospitals through auction;
(b) if so, the reasons therefor;
(c) the details of plots earmarked to be
sold under this scheme alongwith the
number of plots sold so far and the revenue
earned by DDA through it;
†Original notice of the question received in Hindi.

51
(d) whether it is also a fact that such auction
of plots to schools and hospitals would
encourage them for arbitrary conduct; and
(e) if so, the steps being taken by
Government to avoid this situation?
Visit of foreign Secretary to
Sri Lanka
*164. SHRI KALRAJ MISHRA: Will
the PRIME MINISTER be pleased to
state:
(a) whether India's Foreign Secretary
on an invitation from the Srilankan
counterpart, visited Sri Lanka (Colombo)
to settle issues with the LTTE;
(b) if so, the outcome of the visit; and
(c) what further steps if any are being
taken to ensure peace in the neighbouring
country?
Basic amenities at Metro Rail Stations
*165. SHRI KARNENDU BHATTA-
CHARJEE: Will the Minister of URBAN
DEVELOPMENT be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that despite huge
earnings by Delhi Metro Rail Corporation in
Delhi, no basic amenities like drinking water
and toilet facilities, etc. have been provided for
passengers at the Metro Rail Stations;
(b) if so, the reasons for not providing
such facilities for passengers at the Metro
Rail Stations; and
(c) whether Government intend to
provide such facilities and if so, by when
and if not, the reasons therefor?
Plight of slum dwellers in cities
*166. SHRI PRAVEEN RASHTRAPAL:
Will the Minister of HOUSING AND
URBAN POVERTY ALLEVIATION  be
pleased to state:
(a) the details regarding various projects
in hand to improve plight of slum dwellers
in the cities of Delhi, Mumbai, Kolkata,
Hyderabad, Ahmedabad and Chennai;
(b) the norms for providing land/plots
to urban poor as on 31st March, 2006;
(c) whether his Ministry is aware of
various slum demolitions all over the
country by the respective State
Governments; and
(d) whether there is any move in his
Ministry to have an all India policy for slum
improvement and also deciding upon no
removal without alternative arrangements?
National Highways in Sikkim
*167. SHRI O.T. LEPCHA: Will the
Minister of SHIPPING, ROAD
TRANSPORT AND HIGHWAYS be
pleased to state:
(a) the total length of National
Highways constructed in the country
particularly in the State of Sikkim during
the last three years, State-wise;
(b) whether Government have received
any proposal from the States including Sikkim
for construction of National Highways;
(c) if so, the details thereof; and
(d) the details of amount sanctioned and
released for construction of NHs in the
country during this period, State-wise?

52
Re-launch of GSLV/INSAT-4C
*168. SHRI MANOHAR JOSHI: Will
the PRIME MINISTER be pleased to
state:
(a) whether the failure of the Geo
Synchronous Satellite Launch Vehicle
(GSLV) has since been analyzed/probed;
(b) if so, the results thereof;
(c) in what manner this failure would
impact on our  space research programme;
(d) whether Government have set any
schedule for the re-launch of  GSLV/
INSAT-4C; and
(e) if so, the details thereof?
Road accidents on
National Highways
*169. SHRIMATI HEMA MALINI:
Will the Minister of SHIPPING, ROAD
TRANSPORT AND HIGHWAYS be
pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that large number
of fatal accidents are taking place on roads
besides National Highways costing human
lives due to lack of timely medical attention;
(b) the number of such fatal accidents
that took place during the last six months,
State-wise;
(c) whether Government are taking any
steps to save human lives by providing
immediate medical treatment to the victims;
(d) whether there is any such
infrastructure available in our country to
attend to road accident victims like in the
foreign countries;
(e) if so, the details thereof; and
(f) if not, the reasons therefor?
Manufacture of semi-conductors
*170. SHRI CHITTABRATA
MAJUMDAR:
SHRI TAPAN KUMAR SEN:
Will the Minister of
COMMUNICATIONS AND
INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY be
pleased to state:
(a) whether Government are going to
announce a new policy to start the
manufacture of semi-conductors and other
high technology I.T. products;
(b) if so, the salient features of this
policy; and
(c) the time-frame for announcement of
this policy?
Indian labourers in Malaysia
†*171. SHRI JANESHWAR MISHRA:
Will the Minister of OVERSEAS INDIAN
AFFAIRS be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that 37 labourers
of West Bengal have been held as bonded
labourers in Malaysia;
(b) if so, whether it is also a fact that in
the lure of employment, thousands of
people are illegally sent abroad by the travel
agents;
(c) if so, whether Government would
take any steps in order to stop such
incidents and bring back the labourers
illegally sent abroad; and
(d) if so, the details thereof?
India's ambitious space programme
*172. SHRIMATI SHOBHANA
BHARTIA: Will the PRIME MINISTER
be pleased to state:
(a) whether failure of GSLV-F02 in July
†Original notice of the question received in Hindi.

53
2006 was a great setback to India's ambitious
space programme;
(b) if so, whether this disaster has
affected the scientific community and can
delay the country's progress in two crucial
areas;
(c) whether out of 20 scheduled
launches between 1979 and 2005, there
were only four failures;
(d) whether a Committee has been set
up to enquire its failure;
(e) by when the report in this regard is
likely to be submitted; and
(f) whether this will not have any effect
on future  research activities?
Expenditure on National Highways in
Himachal Pradesh
*173. SHRIMATI VIPLOVE
THAKUR: Will the Minister of
SHIPPING, ROAD TRANSPORT AND
HIGHWAYS be pleased to state:
(a) the places in Himachal Pradesh and
other States  where National Highways have
been constructed during the period from
January, 2002 till date alongwith the
expenditure incurred thereon;
(b) the number of National Highways
proposed to be constructed during the
current Five Year Plan, year-wise alongwith
the amount proposed to be spent thereon;
(c) the details of two lane and four lane
highways in the country at present;
(d) whether Government propose to
convert two lane into four lane National
Highways; and
(e) if so, the details thereof?
Help to fight terrorism
*174. SHRI DARA SINGH: Will the
PRIME MINISTER be pleased to state:
(a) whether Government have sought
help from several foreign countries to fight
terrorism in the country;
(b) if so, the details thereof, country-
wise;
(c) whether any final agreements have
been signed with the foreign countries in
this regard during the last two years; and
(d) if so, the details thereof and the extent
to which these have been helpful in
combating the above menace?
Mobile phone towers
*175. SHRI T.T.V. DHINAKARAN:
Will the Minister of
COMMUNICATIONS AND
INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY be
pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that Government
are extending/propose to extend subsidy
for setting up mobile phone towers to
private cellular mobile service providers;
(b) if so, the details thereof; and
(c) the amount likely to be spent on
this as subsidy?
Vehicles launched by ISRO
*176. PROF. P.J. KURIEN: Will the
PRIME MINISTER be pleased to state:
(a) the total number of vehicles launched
by ISRO since 1980;
(b) the number of failures;
(c) in what manner the failure compare
with international standard; and
(d) what steps would be taken to
improve the success rate of launches of
space vehicles and rockets, etc. by ISRO in
the near future?

54
Recommendations of Expert
Committee
*177. SHRI DHARAM PAL
SABHARWAL: Will the Minister of
URBAN DEVELOPMENT be pleased to
state:
(a) the specific recommendations of the
Tejinder Khanna Committee on
unauthorised constructions regarding
allowing/regularizing an additional dwelling
unit besides the three dwelling units
presently allowed on residential plots;
(b) the stand of Government with regard
to these recommendations of the
Committee;
(c) the action taken to accept and notify
the recommendations to bring relief to the
residents of Delhi at the earliest; and
(d) whether the recommendations
would be incorporated in the New Master
Plan for 2021 and by when the new plan is
likely to be notified?
Independent news channel
*178. SHRI RAJEEV SHUKLA: Will
the Minister of INFORMATION AND
BROADCASTING be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that Government
are planning to promote an independent
international news channel based out of
India to counter the bias of existing
international news channels;
(b) if so, the details of the plan and the
action taken in this regard; and
(c) the details of the steps being planned
to ensure autonomy and independence of
the news channels to be launched?
Opening of Nathu-La pass
*179. SHRI S.S. AHLUWALIA: Will
the PRIME MINISTER be pleased to
state:
(a) whether it is a fact that the Nathu-
La pass in Sikkim has been formally opened
recently for passage of export/import traffic
between India and China;
(b) if so, the details thereof, including
the protocol and rule to be observed by
both sides;
(c) the reasons for exposing such a
sensitive region at the border State of our
country, inter alia, to Chinese surveillance;
(d) whether talks are being held with
China for their ceding Indian territory
which continue to remain occupied by them;
and
(e) if so, the status thereof?
Upgradation of State Highways into
National Highways
*180. SHRI JANARDHANA
POOJARY: Will the Minister of
SHIPPING, ROAD TRANSPORT AND
HIGHWAYS be pleased to state:
(a) whether State Governments have
requested the Centre to take over the
responsibility of some of their major
highways for the purpose of upgradation
into National Highways; and
(b) if so, the details thereof and Centre's
reaction thereto, with special reference to
Karnataka and the Bangalore-Hassan-
Mangalore section?

Distribution of power to the
consumers
1019. SHRIMATI SYEDA
ANWARA TAIMUR:
SHRI VIJAY J. DARDA:
Will the PRIME MINISTER be pleased
to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that the third unit
of the Tarapur Atomic Power Project which
would increase the country's nuclear power
generation by one-sixth, is expected to be
declared commercial six months ahead of
schedule;
(b) if so, the details thereof; and
(c) the manner in which the nuclear
power proposed to be distributed to the
consumers?
Transmission system at Rajasthan
1020. SHRI BALAVANT ALIAS
BAL APTE:
SHRI VINAY KATIYAR:
Will the PRIME MINISTER be pleased
to state:
(a) whether Government have a
proposal to set up a transmission system
to supply electricity from the Rajasthan
Atomic Power Project;
(b) if so, the cost of the transmission
system;
(c) the target date set for its completion;
(d) the organization/corporation
entrusted with the task to install the
transmission system; and
(e) the details thereof?

Restart of production at R.A.P.P.
†1021. SHRI LALIT KISHORE
CHATURVEDI: Will the PRIME
MINISTER be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that production
has stopped in the first unit of Rajasthan
Atomic Power Project (R.A.P.P.),
Rawatbhata since October, 2004;
(b) if so, the reasons therefor;
(c) by when the production would
restart; and
(d) if not, the steps being taken by
Government to compensate the loss
suffered by Rajasthan on account of
permanent closure of the first unit of
R.A.P.P.?
FDI proposals
1022. SHRI SURENDRA LATH: Will
the Minister of COAL be pleased to state:
(a) whether a large number of FDI
proposals are under consideration of
Government in the coal mines sector;
(b) if so, the details of the proposals,
State-wise;
(c) the status of those proposals; and
(d) the number of proposals presently
running with FDI?
Valuable waste lying unsold with CIL
1023. SHRI MAHENDRA MOHAN:
Will the Minister of COAL be pleased to
state:
(a) whether it is a fact that Coal India
Ltd. has been holding for years dumps of
18 mt of waste, consisting coal rejects and
midlings, valued at some Rs. 1000 crores,
though it commands a premium in the
domestic market;
(b) if so, the reasons therefor;
(c) whether it is also a fact that while
the private sector miners sell such of their
waste material at about Rs. 600 per tonne,
CIL is unable to get any customer for want
of proper marketing strategy and the
required infrastructure; and
(d) the details of the steps being taken
to dispose of these huge stocks?
Proposal to delink CMPDIL from CIL
1024. SHRI TAPAN KUMAR SEN:
SHRI CHITTABRATA
MAJUMDAR:
Will the Minister of COAL be pleased
to state:
(a) whether there is any proposal to
delink Central Mine Planning and Design
Institute Ltd. (CMPDIL) from Coal India
Ltd. (CIL); and
(b) if so, the reasons therefor?
Outsourcing in CIL to augment
production
1025. SHRI CHITTABRATA
MAJUMDAR:
SHRI TAPAN KUMAR SEN:
Will the Minister of COAL be pleased
to state:
(a) whether outsourcing is being
resorted to augment coal production in
different subsidiaries of Coal India Ltd.;
and
(b) if so, the reasons therefor and
subsidiary-wise quantum of production
through outsourcing?

237
†Original notice of the question received in Hindi.
Demand for increasing royalty on coal
†1026. MS. SUSHILA TIRIYA:
SHRI MOTILAL VORA:
Will the Minister of COAL be pleased
to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that some coal
producing States have been demanding
increase in the rate of royalty on coal for
the last few years;
(b) the names of the States demanding
increase in the rates of royalty alongwith
the existing royalty-rates of the coal; and
(c) the rate and amount of royalty being
extended every year to the coal producing
countries?
Allotment of coal blocks to Jharkhand
†1027. SHRI AJAY MAROO: Will the
Minister of COAL be pleased to state:
(a) whether any request has been
received from Government of Jharkhand
for allotment of coal blocks;
(b) whether Government of Jharkhand
have apprised the Central Government
about their priorities regarding coal blocks;
and
(c) if so, the decision taken by
Government in this regard?
Tribal land taken for coal mining
1028. MS. MABEL REBELLO: Will
the Minister of COAL be pleased to state:
(a) the tribals that have been
dispossessed of their household and
agricultural land due to the coal and other
mining projects in Jharkhand, Chhattisgarh,
Madhya Pradesh and Orissa;
(b) the rehabilitation package offered to
them for the last ten years;
(c) the manner in which the package
would be implemented, the number of such
tribals who originally own the land and have
not been given relief and rehabilitation even
till date, State-wise and year-wise; and
(d) whether the coal companies give
land, cash compensation and also ensure
one job for the families whose land has
been taken away?
CIL joint venture with GAIL
1029. MS. MABEL REBELLO: Will
the Minister of COAL be pleased to state:
(a) whether Coal India Ltd. has been
planning to have a joint venture with GAIL;
(b) if so, the details thereof;
(c) the type of joint venture that is being
planned, the share capital of both the
companies;
(d) the objectives of the Project;
(e) where the Project would be located;
and
(f) the details alongwith the quantum of
funds to be invested?
Plans for structural changes in CIL
†1030. SHRI DATTA MEGHE: Will
the Minister of COAL be pleased to state:
(a) whether Government are considering
a plan which entails structural changes in
Coal India Ltd. to make it a world-class
company;
(b) if so, the types of changes to be
brought about in its structure; and
(c) the measures being taken by
Government to increase availability of coal
in the country?

238
†Original notice of the question received in Hindi.
Private sector participation in coal
sector
1031. SHRIMATI PREMA
CARIAPPA: Will the Minister of COAL
be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that 70 per cent
of the total energy requirement of the
country is met with coal;
(b) if so, the reasons for which
development of new mines has not been
taken up;
(c) whether it is also a fact that the
increasing demand of coal cannot be met
through the public sector alone; and
(d) if so, the steps that have been taken
to encourage private sector in this regard?
MoU with NTPC for power project in
Gujarat
1032. PROF. ALKA BALRAM
KSHATRIYA: Will the Minister of COAL
be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that Government
of Gujarat and NTPC have signed an MoU
for setting up of 1000 MW Power Project
at Pipavav in joint venture;
(b) if so, the present status of the
project;
(c) whether it is also a fact that the
project is held up due to non-allotment of
coal mining block to NTPC by the Ministry
of Coal;
(d) if so, the reasons for delay in
allocation of the coal mining block to NTPC;
and
(e) by when the coal mining block is
likely to be allotted to NTPC?
FDI in Coal
1033. SHRI SITARAM YECHURY:
Will the Minister of COAL be pleased to
state:
(a) whether it is a fact that Government
are opening coal sector for FDI;
(b) if so, the reasons to invite FDI in
coal sector therefor;
(c) whether Government consulted
concerned Trade Unions before opening up
of this sector; and
(d) if so, the details thereof?
Profit of Bihar Telecom Circle
†1034. SHRI MANGANI LAL
MANDAL: Will the Minister of
COMMUNICATIONS AND
INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY be
pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that the estimated
profit of Bihar Telecom Circle under Bharat
Sanchar Nigam Limited has fallen during
the last two years;
(b) if so, the details thereof;
(c) whether it is a fact that the status of
expansion of network of the telephone and
mobile services under Bihar Telecom Circle
is not satisfactory; and
(d) if so, the reasons therefor alongwith
the details thereof?
BPO sector in Orissa
1035. MS. PRAMILA BOHIDAR:
SHRI B.J. PANDA:
Will the Minister of
COMMUNICATIONS AND
INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY be
pleased to state:
(a) whether Government proposes to

239
turn North-Eastern Region into India's next
BPO hot spot;
(b) if so, the details thereof;
(c) whether Government also propose
to develop this sector in the backward,
Orissa State, to improve its economy; and
(d) if so, the details thereof and if not,
the reasons thereof?
Success of 'One India Scheme'
1036. SHRIMATI N.P. DURGA: Will
the Minister of COMMUNICATIONS
AND INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY
be pleased to state:
(a) whether Government have made any
assessment of the success of 'One India
Scheme' launched by BSNL and MTNL;
(b) if so, the details of the assessment;
and
(c) the growth in traffic as well as
addition of new subscribers expected by
BSNL and MTNL?
Poor connectivity of mobile phones
1037. SHRI M.V. MYSURA REDDY:
Will the Minister of COMMUNI-
CATIONS AND INFORMATION
TECHNOLOGY be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that there are
complaints of poor connectivity of the
mobile services provided by MTNL and
which has been deteriorating day by day
thus losing its clientele to private service
providers; and
(b) if so, the action taken to bring the
mobile services provided by MTNL at par
or better as compared to private service
providers?
Rural tele-density in Orissa
1038. MS. PRAMILA BOHIDAR:
SHRI B.J. PANDA:
Will the Minister of COMMUNI-
CATIONS AND INFORMATION
TECHNOLOGY be pleased to state:
(a) whether Orissa's rural tele-density
stands at mearly 0.9 per cent;
(b) whether the State has been left far
behind the target of 7 per cent tele-density
that should have been achieved by 2005;
and
(c) the action of Government to ensure
a respectable rural tele-density alongwith
using ICT to boost development of this
backward region?
Imposition of U.S.O. fee
1039. SHRI B.K. HARIPRASAD: Will
the Minister of COMMUNICATIONS
AND INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY
be pleased to state:
(a) whether the proposed Post Office
(Amendment) Bill, 2006 mandates every
service provider with Rs. 25 lakhs turnover
should pay 10 per cent to help the Postal
Department meets its Universal Service
Obligation;
(b) whether the Competition
Commission of India has asked the
department to study its present cost
structure and assess the burden of serving
remote areas of the country, before
proposing imposition of Universal Service
Obligation fee; and
(c) whether the Commission has asked
the department to explore the possibilities
of cross-subsidising the likely deficit in
serving remote areas from the lucrative
segment services of the department?

240
Indian Post Office (Amendment) Bill
1040. SHRI B.K. HARIPRASAD: Will
the Minister of COMMUNICATIONS
AND INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY
be pleased to state:
(a) whether the Competition
Commission of India (CCA) has found the
provisions in the draft Indian Post Office
(Amendment) Bill barring courier firms
from carrying articles weighing less than
300 gms, as violative of the spirit of
competition;
(b) whether the category of articles
weighing less than 300 gms accounts for 95
per cent of all mailed correspondence in
the country; and
(c) whether the Commission has
contended that such a move would foster
State monopoly and deny a level playing
field for the private sector courier firms?
Call drops and bad connectivity due to
interconnection
1041. SHRI VIJAY J. DARDA: Will
the Minister of COMMUNICATIONS
AND INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY
be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that TRAI has
rapped BSNL for high level of congestion
on calls from networks of private mobile
operators to its point of interconnection
resulting in call drops and bad connectivity;
(b) if so, whether any study has been
made to find out exact position, as
otherwise any low grade of service to mobile
telephone users will discourage use of this
service especially in rural areas;
(c) whether there has been any delay on
the part of BSNL in provisioning of one
leased line on which 30 simultaneous calls
can be made; and
(d) the steps have been taken to
streamline the systems so that, such a
situation is not allowed to linger on thus
putting adverse effect on the service to
mobile users?
Women employees in IT sector
†1042. MISS ANUSUIYA UIKEY: Will
the Minister of COMMUNICATIONS
AND INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY
be pleased to state:
(a) the number of women employees in
the IT sector at present;
(b) whether the number of these women
employees have increased during the last
five years; and
(c) if so, the details thereof, State-wise?
Blocking of Website
1043. DR. M.A.M. RAMASWAMY:
Will the Minister of
COMMUNICATIONS AND
INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY be
pleased to state:
(a) whether Government have asked the
Internet Service Providers (ISPs) to block
around 17-18 Websites on the Internet;
(b) if so, the details of sites to be blocked;
(c) the reasons therefor;
(d) the ISPs who have blocked the
Websites; and
(e) the ISPs, who have not blocked the
Websites?
†Original notice of the question received in Hindi.

241
Breach of privacy by private operators
1044. SHRI JANARDHANA
POOJARY: Will the Minister of
COMMUNICATIONS AND
INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY be
pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that a number of
private operators have been issued license
